resolved_by: The Supreme Court resolved the split in Rutherford, 146 S. Ct. 1330, holding that a nonretroactive change in sentencing law is not an extraordinary and compelling reason for compassionate release, which the Eighth Circuit applied here.
issue: Can a nonretroactive change in sentencing law, such as a longer sentence that would no longer be imposed, count as an extraordinary and compelling reason for compassionate release under USSG § 1B1.13(b)(6)?

sides.position: A nonretroactive change in sentencing law is not an extraordinary and compelling reason for compassionate release, so § 1B1.13(b)(6) cannot override circuit precedent holding otherwise.
cases: United States v. Loggins, Nos. 24-1488, 24-1569 (8th Cir. 2026)

this_court: Does not take a split position; it follows Rutherford and holds that the Defendants' arguments are foreclosed, consistent with its Crandall precedent.
quote: A circuit split developed over this issue.
cite: United States v. Isaac Loggins, Jr., No. 24-1488, 24-1569 (8th Cir. 2026)
